newsitem.title: USA: Deregulation key to Japan economy-Westinghouse CEO.
newsitem.headline: Deregulation key to Japan economy-Westinghouse CEO.

text.p: Japan needs to deregulate its economy deeply and quickly for its own good, Westinghouse Electric Corp Chairman Michael Jordan said on Tuesday.
Jordan, who is also chairman of the U.S.-Japan Business Council, said Americans were impressed that deregulation of the Japanese economy was "now on the front burner."

"Most of us here on the U.S. side strongly believe that Japan needs to deregulate, and deregulate deeply and quickly for its own good. You have run out of economic levers to boost the economy," Jordan said.

"We think deregulation will do wonders for domestic demand in Japan, thus perhaps blunting the need for a fierce export war again," Jordan told hundreds of U.S. and Japanese business people at a conference in San Francisco organized by the U.S.-Japan and Japan-U.S. business councils.

He said interest rates in Japan had been at an all-time low for several years and investment had not fueled growth. "Short of the Bank of Japan paying businesses to borrow and invest, there is nothing the Japanese government can do on the monetary front," he said.
Jordan said the "old standby" of fiscal stimulus was out of the question. The recent rise in the consumption tax would put a drag on the economy and risk recession, he said.

"The recent decline in the yen against the dollar seems to have convinced some that Japan can export its way back to prosperity, but a short-term rise in the bilateral trade deficit makes it difficult for Americans to grasp why Japan has not done more to fix its economy," Jordan said.
